title: Spectroscopy validates machine-selected populations of obscured active galaxies
summary: Using a sample selected by unsupervised machine learning on optical and mid-infrared photometry, the team obtained 178 MMT spectra and found the brighter class was 85% Type I active galactic nuclei (AGN), with <3% non-AGN contamination, while a fainter class was 65% Type II AGN with 15% contamination, mainly star-forming galaxies. The follow-up showed that the machine-selected classes recover redder and more obscured AGN populations than typical optical spectroscopic samples.
ai_technology: Unsupervised UMAP and DBSCAN photometric AGN selection pipeline
organization: University of Arizona; Princeton University; MMT Observatory

evidence.tested: Using a sample selected by unsupervised machine learning on optical and mid-infrared photometry, the team obtained 178 MMT spectra and found the brighter class was 85% Type I active galactic nuclei (AGN), with <3% non-AGN contamination, while a fainter class was 65% Type II AGN with 15% contamination, mainly star-forming galaxies.
evidence.unknown: This is a follow-up validation of two machine-selected candidate classes, not a claim that every cataloged object is confirmed. Spectroscopy recovered redshifts for 139 of 178 spectra; the fainter Type II class was limited to the brightest 75% of candidates and had 15% contamination, primarily from star-forming galaxies. The unsupervised pipeline is described in related work listed as in preparation in this paper; findings here are bounded to the spectroscopically analyzed sample.
evidence.ai_role: The selection pipeline applied UMAP dimensionality reduction and DBSCAN clustering to optical and mid-infrared colors and morphology, with matched spectroscopy and X-ray information used to identify AGN candidate classes. Those classes defined the targets for Hectospec follow-up; the paper then used optical spectra, emission-line diagnostics, and spectral stacking to test their AGN content. The AI selected the candidate populations, while spectroscopic diagnostics established the reported classifications.
